evidence.dominant_driver: Bullock says supply shocks complicate monetary policy, policy must prevent second-round inflation effects, and the AI investment boom is adding excess demand to the Australian economy.

market_expectations.expected_value: A September 29 RBA hike was already heavily priced, with estimates around 90-95%; all four major Australian banks expected a 25bp hike.
market_expectations.distribution_notes: The remarks reinforce an already-hawkish path rather than introduce a wholly new hike scenario.

absorption.reason: The hike itself was already close to fully priced before Bullock spoke. A reliable post-event AUS200 print was not available at decision time, so only the policy-pricing component can be judged as absorbed.

immediate.rationale: The remarks are about 45 minutes old and a September hike was already heavily priced; no reliable post-event index reaction is available to justify chasing a short.

next_session.rationale: If Australian yields/AUD reprice higher into the RBA meeting, valuation pressure should remain a headwind for AUS200.

15m.rationale: The remarks are about 45 minutes old and a September hike was already heavily priced; no reliable post-event index reaction is available to justify chasing a short.

1h.rationale: Hawkish inflation language conflicts with the session's strong global tech/risk-on lead and lower oil backdrop.

4h.rationale: Explicit concern about second-round effects and AI-driven excess demand strengthens the case for restrictive policy and can weigh on rate-sensitive Australian equities.

next_session.rationale: If Australian yields/AUD reprice higher into the RBA meeting, valuation pressure should remain a headwind for AUS200.

predictions.mechanism: More persistent inflation and AI-driven excess demand increase the probability/duration of restrictive RBA policy, raising discount rates and pressuring domestic rate-sensitive sectors.
predictions.invalidation: AUS200 holding/breaking the session high while Australian yields and AUD fail to rise would invalidate the 4h downside thesis; a materially dovish clarification would also invalidate it.
predictions.counter_case: The September hike is already nearly fully priced, lower oil reduces the inflation impulse, and global AI/tech risk appetite can dominate the local rates headwind.
